settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards: identifying the Pareto optimal set under a preference cone.
unmapped: Vector-valued rewards with L objectives per arm, mean matrix M in R^{L x K}
Goal: exactly identify the Pareto optimal set / Pareto optimal policy w.r.t. a known polyhedral preference cone C
The learner knows the preference cone C and the noise covariance Sigma = Diag(sigma_1^2..sigma_L^2)
Single-parameter exponential family per objective with variance bounded by 1; noise also stated sub-Gaussian
settings.definition_quote: In PrePEx, a learner can access a bandit instance with $K$ arms. Each arm $k \in [K]$ corresponds to a reward distribution $P_k$ over $\mR^L$ with unknown mean $M_k \in \mR^{L}$ and known covariance $\Sigma$ ... the goal of the learner is to identify a Pareto optimal policy in $\Pi^{\ast}$ given an instance $M$ and a preference cone $\cC$ while observing only noisy rewards from the arms, and also using as few observations as possible.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards: Pareto set identification under a preference cone.
unmapped: Vector rewards N(mu_a, Sigma) with diagonal known covariance over L objectives
settings.definition_quote: In Gaussian bandits, we assume that the reward vectors of arm $a \in [K]$ are generated from a multivariate Gaussian distribution $\cN(\mu_a, \Sigma)$, where the covariance is a diagonal matrix: $\Sigma \eqdef \mathrm{Diag}(\sigma_1^2, \ldots, \sigma_L^2)$.

symbols.T_MC: characteristic time of the PrePEx instance (M, C): inverse of sup_w inf_{pi, pi*} inf_{M~ in boundary of alternative set} inf_{z in C} sum_k w_k KL(z^T M_k, z^T M~_k)

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Given a bandit model $M \in \instset$, a preference cone $\cC$, and a confidence level $\delta \in [0,1)$, the expected stopping time of any $(1-\delta)$-correct PrePEx algorithm, to identify the Pareto Optimal Set is \mE[\tau] \ge \cT_{M,\cC}\log\left(\frac{1}{2.4\delta}\right)

results.notes: Characteristic time defined via a nested sup-inf over allocations, policies, alternative instances on the boundary and preference vectors z in C.

symbols.T_Gauss: Gaussian characteristic time, inverse = inf over neighbouring policies pi of pi* and min over z in C\{0} of (z^T M (pi*-pi))^2 / (2 Tr(Sigma) ||pi*-pi||_2^2)

conditions: Gaussian rewards with known diagonal covariance Sigma

source.label: thm:gaussian-bandit
source.quote: The inverse of characteristic time, i.e. $(\cT^{\mathrm{Gauss}}_{M,\cC})^{-1}$, for an instance $(M, \cC)$ is \inf_{\pi \in N(\pi^*), \pi^* \in \Pi^*(M)}\min_{z \in \cC\setminus\{0\}} \frac{(z^{\top}M(\pi^*-\pi))^2}{2\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)\|\pi^*-\pi\|_2^2}

results.notes: Theorem only characterises the characteristic time for Gaussians; the lower bound E[tau] >= T log(1/(2.4 delta)) follows by plugging into Theorem (thm:lower-bound). Part 1 (form of most confusing instance) not recorded separately.

symbols.Tbar_MC: characteristic time of the convex relaxation (alternative set replaced by its convex hull) of the PrePEx lower bound

tuning: stopping threshold beta(t,delta) = sum_k 3 ln(1+ln N_{k,t}) + K*T(ln(1/delta)/K)

source.label: thm:upper-tns
source.quote: For any $\alpha > 0$ and $c(t,\delta)$ defined in~\eqref{eqn:chernoff-stopping}, we have that the stopping time satisfies \lim_{\delta \rightarrow 0} \frac{\mE[\stoptime]}{\log\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)} \le \overline{\chartime} \ \forall \ M \in \mR^{L \times K}

results.notes: Matches only the convexified lower bound (paper notes this is not strictly asymptotically optimal). Appendix restatement has an extra factor alpha (>=1) and liminf; main text statement recorded. PreTS also (1-delta)-correct via Lemma/Theorem on stopping.
